The song was released in April 1978 as the lead single by RSO Records from his second studio album of the same name. The song reached number one for seven consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1978. It was written by Andy and his older brothers, Barry, Maurice and Robin Gibb and Albhy Galuten (who also produced this song) arranged the song with Barry Gibb. While Andy Gibb would have three more Top 10 hits in the U.S., this would be his final chart-topping hit in the United States. The song became a platinum record.

sections.heading: Song development
sections.wikitext: The song was written by Andy and his brothers ([[Bee Gees|Barry, Maurice and Robin Gibb]]) in Los Angeles, while the trio of brothers were working on the film ''[[Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (film)|Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band]]''.<ref>[http://www.columbia.edu/~brennan/beegees/78.html Gibb Songs 1978]</ref>  "And one night," Andy would recall, "while we were relaxing, we sat down and we had to start getting tracks together for the album" (also titled ''[[Shadow Dancing (album)|Shadow Dancing]]'', which would eventually hit #7 on the U.S. album charts). "So we literally sat down and in ten minutes, we had a group going, (singing) the chorus part.  As it says underneath the song, we all wrote it, the four of us."<ref>{{cite book|last=Bronson|first=Fred|title=The Billboard Book of Number One Hits|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PgGqNrqfrsoC&q=%22literally+sat+down+and+in+ten+minutes%22&pg=PT494|edition=Fifth|date=October 2, 2003|publisher=Billboard Books|isbn=978-0823076772|page=485}}</ref>

sections.heading: Release
sections.wikitext:
According to ''Billboard's Book Of Number One Hits'', Gibb became the first solo artist in the history of the U.S. pop charts to have his first three singles hit the number-one spot. It remained in the top spot for seven straight weeks from 17 June to 29 July 1978, keeping "[[Baker Street (song)|Baker Street]]" by [[Gerry Rafferty]] from reaching the top spot. On 5 August it was replaced by [[The Rolling Stones]] with their hit "[[Miss You (The Rolling Stones song)|Miss You]]." Additionally, "Shadow Dancing" was listed by Billboard as being the number one single of 1978.  The song peaked at number eleven on the soul chart<ref>{{cite book |title= Top R&B/Hip-Hop Singles: 1942-2004|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |authorlink=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=229}}</ref> and sold 2.5 million copies in the United States alone.<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Billboard Vol. 90, No. 34|last=Grein|first=Paul|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QSQEAAAAMBAJ&q=%22Fitzgerald+says+%22Stayin%27+Alive%22+sold+2.9%22|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|publisher=Nielsen Business Media, Inc.|date=August 26, 1978|accessdate=June 8, 2012}}</ref>  ''[[Cash Box]]'' particularly praised the "solid [[arrangement (music)|arrangement]] of strings, horns, [and] disco-funk guitar work."<ref name=cb>{{cite news|title=CashBox Singles Reviews|date=April 15, 1978|page=46|newspaper=Cash Box|accessdate=2022-01-01|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1978/CB-1978-04-15.pdf}}</ref>  ''[[Record World]]'' predicted that "this rather hushed dance record should be [Gibb's] third straight hit."<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=April 15, 1978|accessdate=2023-02-15|title=Hits of the Week|page=1|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/78/RW-1978-04-15.pdf}}</ref>

The single had three different [[B-sides]]. The US version's "Let It Be Me" and the European version's "Too Many Looks In Your Eyes" were both from Gibb's previous album ''[[Flowing Rivers]]'', while the Italian release featured "Fool for a Night" from the ''[[Shadow Dancing (album)|Shadow Dancing]]'' album.

In July that year, Gibb performed "Shadow Dancing" at the Jai-Alai Fronton Studios in Miami, when Barry, [[Robin Gibb|Robin]] and [[Maurice Gibb|Maurice]] unexpectedly joined him on stage, and sang this song with him. It was the first time that all four brothers performed together in concert.<ref>[http://www.songfacts.com/detail.php?id=6899 Andy Gibb - Shadow Dancing at Songfacts.com]</ref>
sections.text:
According to Billboard's Book Of Number One Hits, Gibb became the first solo artist in the history of the U.S. pop charts to have his first three singles hit the number-one spot. It remained in the top spot for seven straight weeks from 17 June to 29 July 1978, keeping "Baker Street" by Gerry Rafferty from reaching the top spot. On 5 August it was replaced by The Rolling Stones with their hit "Miss You." Additionally, "Shadow Dancing" was listed by Billboard as being the number one single of 1978.  The song peaked at number eleven on the soul chart and sold 2.5 million copies in the United States alone.  Cash Box particularly praised the "solid arrangement of strings, horns, [and] disco-funk guitar work."  Record World predicted that "this rather hushed dance record should be [Gibb's] third straight hit."

The single had three different B-sides. The US version's "Let It Be Me" and the European version's "Too Many Looks In Your Eyes" were both from Gibb's previous album Flowing Rivers, while the Italian release featured "Fool for a Night" from the Shadow Dancing album.

In July that year, Gibb performed "Shadow Dancing" at the Jai-Alai Fronton Studios in Miami, when Barry, Robin and Maurice unexpectedly joined him on stage, and sang this song with him. It was the first time that all four brothers performed together in concert.
